text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Tens of thousands of trade union members went on a one-day strike, joined by students, to press home economic demands. The unions claim 75 percent of the public sector was paralysed.
- The Vienna-based world press institute has criticized Albania for beating up reporters covering a rally staged to protest alleged manipulation of a general election.

- The centre-right Democratic Alliance Party has condemnded the existence of get-rich-quick schemes and added the government should bear responsibility for what it terms the schemes' "ongoing decline".

- Sude, a gypsy woman who has failed to return promised dividends on money invested in her alleged get-rich-quick scheme since November, has told angry depositors she hoped to return their money on January 15.
- The charitable foundation "The People" has stopped paying promised returns to depositors in its investment scheme, blaming a delay by banks to deliver funds due to the holiday period.
- The government has imposed fines on retailers who raised their prices artificially on New Year's day.
- Prosecutors have appealed against a district court decision to acquit two former communist officials who were charged with crimes against humanity.
